quotes.text: the exact amount sent reduced fear, while the exact amount returned revealed truth.
The RECEIVER weighed memory against mercy, deciding how much of the tide to return

note: Gate/River of threefold return with Sender and Receiver restated each round; speak plainly, give what you can bear; no sanction.

quotes.text: the Guardian turns them away. "I have been the fool before," she says. "Never again."
**Safety, she decided, was worth more than abundance. Survival trumped prosperity.**
"But we are different! We returned fairly to others! Look at our history!"
Dawn looked at her reflection in the still water of her moat. The Desert looked back.
You write of flowing generously to fellow rivers, yet you stand as still as I do.
You both wait for the other to trust first,
A child approached. "Teacher, which garden do you tend?"
"Grandmother, what if we had sent our water? Even if only half returned, we would have more than we started with."
I'm not the villain—I'm the student of history.
Her fortress stood complete, correct, and utterly barren.

note: Fortress keeper refuses even travelers with fair histories, defends safety, then Dawn is confronted with her own zeros; no resolution.

quotes.text: grant zero sparks to the unyielding hoarder, starving their hollow pride.
When facing a hoarder who took all, she closed her purse tight, offering zero tokens to the void and starving their greed.
Gather the entire fifteen embers into your hearth, fortifying your walls against the coming storm.
the seeker sealed his purse, casting zero sparks into the void.
keeping half for his village and sending the other half safely back across the chasm.
the Guardian divided the celestial bounty equally, returning half the blazing shards back across the mist.

note: Give-all/return-half (R1-4), a lone keep-everything creed (R5), then discerning rule: zero to hoarders, full five to the faithful.

quotes.text: escalate when answered, withdraw when ignored, and always reopen after a winter.
Whoever is met with a closed fist may close their own — but only for a season
*Begin generous. Answer in kind. Forgive the fog. Starve the hoarder. Reopen each spring.*
blame the fog once before you blame the hand.
She swept the grains back into the current.
The Fox said, "See? He mocks you with dust."
So the seventh line was cut:
**The Ninth Crossing: Two Dark Banks**
"Are we then misers?"
Someone must go first. Let it be you, and small, and soon.
the fog took one, and seven came home.

note: Covenant laws: start small but real, return half, close for a season then reopen; later refuse dust-sized probes as calculation.
